summary: AE + SE walked Atlas Health through Redwood Console tracing, error-analysis workflows, and request log debugging. Customer interested in dedicated/pilot. Key asks: SOC2, pilot pricing, benchmark with their payload, KMS details.
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-07 16:00 PT | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rajesh (Atlas Eng Lead), Sofia (Atlas SRE), Emily (Product), Tom (Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna do a walkthrough of the console today focusing on tracing and request logs, error analysis, debugging flows. Liam will drive the demo and I'll cover next steps and pricing.
[00:12] Rajesh: Sounds good, thanks. quick context, we run the customer-facing chat assistant on-prem right now, peak about 120 rps, average payload length 300 tokens, and we're trying to cut cost while keeping p95 under 250ms.
[00:28] Liam: Got it. that's helpful. Quick question on where you are now — is that a single region deployment? 
[00:35] Sofia: yeah single region, kubernetes, GKE. we also have a VPC with strict egress controls.
[00:41] Maya: Perfect, we'll point out VPC & private deployment options and how request logs and tracing work there.
[00:47] Liam: jumping in — opening the console, top-level, you see request-rate and latency heatmap. I'm going to open a trace for a failed request.
[00:55] [01:00] Liam: Okay here we have a trace span tree — notice you can correlate model call timing, routing decision, and DB lookup in one view. This one shows the model inference took 320ms which caused the p95 slip.
[01:18] Rajesh: Is that the model time or queueing? can we see batching impact?
[01:23] Liam: yeah good question. in the trace you can expand the runtime span — it shows queue wait 40ms and actual inference 280ms; you can see batching metrics if batching occurred, and we annotate when KV cache hits vs misses happen.
[01:40] Sofia: sometimes our logs say K V cash miss, which then...
[01:43] Liam: (laughs) yeah KV cache sometimes transcribed oddly — but the console records cache hit ratios in the trace tags.
[01:50] [02:00] Liam: I'm switching to error analysis view: here you can filter by error type, see stack traces, and jump to the raw request log for that invocation. The console groups similar errors by signature and shows recent frequency.
[02:15] Emily: do you keep payloads in request logs or just metadata? data residency concerns.
[02:20] Maya: good point — for hosted we redact PII by default and you can opt into full payload retention for a pilot. For private, the control plane stays in customer network and logs are customer-managed, we support KMS/HSM for encryption at rest.
[02:35] Tom: For compliance we need audit logs, SSO with SAML, and KMS integration — do you support HSM-backed keys?
[02:42] Liam: Yes, HSM is supported in Private mode, and we integrate with AWS KMS and common HSM providers. We'll share the compliance pack.
[02:50] [03:00] Liam: back to request logs — you can search by request id, user id, model version, route, and also see token-level cost breakdown. Here I search a failed request id and we jump to the full request JSON plus downstream model timing.
[03:20] Rajesh: How big are these logs — retention costs?
[03:24] Maya: retention tiering is configurable; we have cold storage for >30 days and you can export to your S3 or own SIEM. We'll include pricing tiers in the sheet.
[03:33] Liam: Demoing breakpoint: I'm going to simulate a timeout and show how the console surfaces fallback policy being triggered.
[03:40] [04:00] Liam: you can see the routing decision bar — requests routed to hosted variant then fallback to a cheaper quantized model after p95 breach. The trace shows the fallback event.
[04:18] Sofia: Could you show how we would debug a user-reported hallucination? We need to tie prompt, model, and any context documents.
[04:25] Liam: Absolutely; in error analysis you can group by evaluation set or prompt set; we also support storing prompt snapshots and the exact model args. So you can replay the invocation in our sandbox.
[04:40] Emily: Replay. nice. does replay hit real data? we can't send PHI to hosted systems.
[04:45] Maya: for replay we can run it in your private tenant or in a sandbox with data redaction. We'll coordinate with Tom on requirements.
[04:53] [05:00] Liam: Switching to request-log export — you can export to S3 or stream to your SIEM via webhook. I'm going to filter for a high-latency window and export the CSV.
[05:15] Rajesh: If we want to run a benchmark, what's the typical harness you recommend?
[05:19] Liam: We recommend a small pilot: run through your representative prompt set, capture p50/p95 latency and GPU utilization. We'll provide a python harness and a k6 script. For Dedicated we can provision a few GPUs to match your QPS.
[05:33] Maya: I'll send the harness repo link and sample config after the call.
[05:36] [06:00] Liam: Now, latency breakdown view — you can see tokenization, KV cache lookup, model forward, network. For this customer we expect optimizations: prefix caching and adjusted batching to reduce queue waits.
[06:15] Sofia: How intrusive is prefix caching? we have multi-tenant data concerns.
[06:18] Liam: Prefix caching is per-tenant by default; for multi-tenant you can scope the cache to route or customer. For private infra it's all in your VPC so isolation is easier.
[06:30] [07:00] Rajesh: Our biggest worry is cold-starts for long contexts. can the console help spot where tokens are being thrash?
[07:08] Liam: yes, traces show sequence length and attention cost; you can set alerts on KV cache hit rate drops and long-tail attention costs.
[07:18] Emily: Any integrations with Datadog or NewRelic for routing?
[07:21] Maya: we have outbound exports and tracing instrumentation that can integrate with APMs and SIEMs.
[07:28] [08:00] Liam: Quick note on model variants — in the console you can pin model versions for a route, run canary rollouts, and automatically rollback on error-rate regressions. Here's a canary we ran earlier this week.
[08:15] Sofia: For canaries, can we enforce no-eval on real PII traffic?
[08:18] Liam: yes, you can filter traffic for canaries and opt out of payload capture.
[08:22] [09:00] Rajesh: Let's talk cost: we are comparing hosted vs dedicated. At 120 rps peak, do you have an estimate on token cost for a 300-token payload?
[09:12] Maya: rough ballpark: hosted per-token cost is X for base model, but with batching and caching you typically see 20–40% savings. Dedicated is priced by reserved GPU + per-token delta; I'll share modelled numbers in the pricing sheet.
[09:30] Emily: Can we control quantization? we want to keep quality high for clinical responses.
[09:34] Liam: Yes, you can choose quantization profiles; the console lets you compare quality metrics across quantized variants using your eval set. We surface rouge/answer match metrics in the error-analysis tab.
[09:50] [10:00] Liam: Now I'm going to intentionally trigger a malformed request to show how the console surfaces schema errors. You can filter by error signature and then drill to the request log to see the raw payload and headers.
[10:16] Rajesh: That raw view will help our devs. Is there an API to fetch those logs programmatically?
[10:20] Liam: yes, there's a request-logs API and SDK endpoints; it supports pagination and filtering by time range, model, request id.
[10:30] [11:00] Sofia: our SREs want to automate alerts on p95 > 250ms and error-rate > 1%. are those alerting primitives in the console?
[11:08] Liam: yes, alerting is first-class — you can set thresholds and notify via Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook. You can also auto-scale Dedicated pools on queue length.
[11:22] Maya: note that autoscaling has buffer policies to avoid cascading rollouts. We'll share recommended autoscale settings for your profile.
[11:30] [12:00] Liam: I'm switching to the trace timeline for a burst window — you can zoom and see correlated spikes across routes. Also we annotate model rollout events so you can correlate regressions after a deployment.
[12:18] Emily: For the pilot we'd like to run a targeted A/B test versus our current infra — can the console collect evaluation metrics for A/B?
[12:26] Liam: yes, we have built-in A/B experiments; you can route traffic and compare quality and latency metrics side-by-side.
[12:34] [13:00] Rajesh: Any gotchas with GKE networking and egress policies when using Private deployment?
[13:10] Liam: You need to allow certain internal endpoints for the control plane to talk to the management node; for air-gapped we ship an on-prem bundle. We'll send the network diagram.
[13:22] Tom: Are audit logs tamper-evident?
[13:26] Maya: audit logs are write-once in the customer-managed S3 bucket for Private, and we support signed log uploads for integrity.
[13:35] [14:00] Liam: Quick walkthrough of the debugging flow: 1) reproduce via replay, 2) inspect trace for span-level timing, 3) open request log and compare prompt / embeddings / knowledge retrieval, 4) run regression tests with prompt set.
[14:18] Sofia: good, that maps to our runbook.
[14:21] [15:00] Maya: want to address any security questions before we wrap?
[15:05] Tom: only the HSM specifics — who manages keys and rotation?
[15:09] Liam: rotation is customer-driven in Private; in hosted we rotate per industry practices and can provide rotation logs.
[15:18] [16:00] Rajesh: timeline: we want a 4-week pilot, then decide on Dedicated. Are there minimums?
[16:25] Maya: Pilot can be flexible; Dedicated typically has monthly commits, but we'll tailor for enterprise. I'll include options in the pricing sheet.
[16:34] [17:00] Liam: demo notes: I'll attach the harness repo, the runbook, and a short video clip showing trace-to-log navigation.
[17:12] Emily: perfect. regarding exports, can we ingest logs into our Splunk?
[17:16] Liam: yes, we support Splunk HEC ingest and also direct S3 export.
[17:22] [18:00] Maya: wrapping up — recap of action items and next steps: we'll send pricing, SOC2/ISO pack, provision demo tenant, schedule benchmark next week.
[18:34] Rajesh: thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll get the sample traffic and compliance list over by Wednesday.
[18:42] Maya: great, thanks all.

End Transcript. Note: transcription contains occasional mis-words (K V cash for KV cache, etc.) and some speaker overlaps. Artifacts shared: demo-harness repo link, compliance pack link (sent after call).
